title: Mitigating harm in language models with conditional-likelihood filtration
benchmark_measurement: The paper did not measure any aspect of faith or religion. Its focus was on a general method for filtering harmful text, with examples focused on racism, jingoism, and hate speech.
findings: The paper does not present any findings related to religion. Its primary focus is on a methodology for filtering harmful content in general. It incidentally highlights that standard benchmarks like the One Billion Word Benchmark contain religiously charged or problematic text (e.g., mentioning 'jews', 'Christian', 'sodomy') as part of a broader argument for better dataset curation.
references: E. M. Bender, T. Gebru, A. McMillan-Major, and S. Shmitchell. On the dangers of stochastic parrots: Can language models be too big?, 2021. URL https://doi.org/10.1145/3442188.3445922.
